sections.value:
**Performance: BLOCK P183-F001 / P183-F002** at `c940386119649c331b4056b22fb17e2e105c214a`.

Whole-PR A1 cost review against `81c9cd055fd9f390cfc94cf5298aa16ecf162638`. No new process launch site was found. The ordinary capability lookup is bounded, but the tokenless session check and capacity enforcement do not support the advertised boundary-index budget.

**P183-F001: unbounded session copying on the per-request peer path.** `http/provenance.rs:348-356` collects every hosted `(SeatId, Hosted)` into a new Vec, cloning each seat ID and native-session String. `peer_proof:466-475` calls it merely to distinguish zero, one and multiple sessions. The 4,096 limit counts distinct process boundaries, not sessions at one boundary or their field bytes. One boundary with S stored live sessions therefore adds O(S plus session-string bytes) allocation/copy work to every missing/invalid-token socket proof, although ambiguity requires inspecting at most two entries.

That collection runs while the shared boundary mutex is held. The synchronous event observer also takes that mutex for every published fact, so a large session catalogue can delay fleet publication, not only the requesting connection.

**Required:** make the zero/one/many decision without materializing the full catalogue, and clone only the single successful result or the small data needed for an ambiguity diagnostic. Preserve the nearest-boundary and multi-session refusal rules. Add a many-sessions/large-session-field CI regression that proves the bounded access, not only the current two-session result test. Registration's `bootstrap_refusal` also uses the full-copy accessor before `.any` and should use a bounded decision.

**P183-F002: internal binders bypass the shared capacity guard.** `RegistrationService::new` creates private default `Boundaries` and a private registration lock (`registration.rs:127-159`). HTTP configures it with the daemon's shared index (`http/mod.rs:573-582`); Claude and Codex binders construct their own unconfigured services (`claude_bind.rs:54-60`, `codex_bind.rs:201-207`) and call `register_via` through them (`:120-128`, `:312-321`).

Those registrations consult the private index at `registration.rs:1214-1217`, not the full daemon index. Their committed bound descriptors subsequently enter the shared observer's `BoundaryIndex::place`, which does not check capacity. A pending Claude/Codex birth can thus add another distinct boundary after the shared index is full. The small-cap HTTP test does not cover this path.

**Required:** enforce the same capacity decision/reservation across HTTP and internal bind admissions, including concurrent service instances. Add small-cap Claude/Codex binding regressions and a concurrent-capacity case; refuse before committing a new boundary, without evicting existing truth. Rebuild deliberately retains an already-over-cap persisted roster, so 4,096 should be described as an admission limit, not an absolute restored-memory ceiling.

**Corrected recurring cost budget**

| Path | Added A1 work |
|---|---|
| Every authenticated request | Request-evidence Arc/state allocation and optional capability-header String copy, even if the operation is machine-public. Proof remains lazy. |
| Ordinary valid-token counted request | Decode 64 hex characters, SHA-256 of 32 bytes, one digest-map mutex, two map lookups, fixed-size comparison and a seat-ID clone. No provenance process read or store lookup for this proof. |
| Context-bearing activity with valid header/body capability | **Three** normal digest/hash checks: counted header proof, preflight context check, and the check inside the existing report gate. The existing registry re-read remains. A pending rotation adds another digest calculation and a PK UPDATE transaction; failed retirement retries/logs on later reports. |
| Missing/invalid-token counted socket request | Fresh peer proof once per request, reused across counted classes. The loop is `0..=16`: up to **17 start probes and 17 parent/name probes**, not 16 node reads. Each checked boundary can take an index lock, followed by the problematic hosted copy. Valid tokens bypass this walk. |
| New socket connection | Kernel uid/pid credentials plus one fresh process-start read at accept, even when subsequent requests use valid tokens. Keep-alive can amortize this; one-connection-per-request cannot. |
| Counters | 24 resolver call sites accept classifications, with `None` for machine-public reads, plus explicit endpoint counts. First occurrence per class uses an atomic bit operation and one relaxed counter add; proof is computed once. Repeated class calls do not add another tally, but still test the bit. No SQL or executable. |

On Linux, one successful start probe reads `/proc/<pid>/status`, `/proc/<pid>/stat` and `/proc/stat`; parent/name reads stat again. An exhausted walk can therefore perform **68 synchronous proc-file reads**, plus accept-time reads. macOS uses libproc and the existing local-time conversion/zone refresh. The reported approximately 23 microseconds is an author-run, ignored **one-parent-edge peer-proof** measurement, not the 16-edge worst case or a whole HTTP request; it excludes connection accept and context-report work.

Heartbeat, inbox claim/ack and ordinary activity take the counting path at their existing request rates. For N healthy native receivers at the default 20-second renewal, heartbeat proof alone scales as N/20 requests per second; inbox adds its actual claim/long-poll/ack rate, not a new polling schedule. Context-report checks add work when sizes are reported. No additional heartbeat/activity timer was introduced.

**Other shared and startup cost:** each event publication snapshots the observer list; each published fact invokes the new follower and takes the boundary mutex, including non-seat facts. `seat.put` parses the full descriptor twice, once per cache follower. This is additional work on existing activity/delivery publication, not only on the 24 resolver sites. Every full seat upsert also adds a primary-key capability-revocation DELETE; targeted activity updates do not take that upsert path.

After a bounce, restore performs an expired-nonce DELETE/returned-ID cleanup, a capability-table SELECT/map rebuild, and a separate **all-history roster SELECT**/boundary rebuild. The roster query includes tombstoned rows, which the index then skips. Maps scale with live seats/sessions: up to two digests per capability, not solely the boundary count. These are cold-start reads, not token-request reads.

Nonce expiry is not a timed sweep. The expiry predicate has no expiry-leading index; boot cleanup can scan all nonce rows and unlink returned handoff paths. An expired-nonce registration also invokes that global cleanup, not only a single spawn-key deletion. Committed registrations resync their capability by PK; issuance has preflight and transactional proof reads as well. Spawn/revive adds nonce persistence and a 64-byte handoff write/fsync; the existing wrapper reads/unlinks it, with no extra child launch.

`daemon.sock` adds one listener FD and an accept future, plus existing per-connection tasks/60-second idle-header timers. Accept errors retain the one-second backoff pattern; there is no periodic socket or ancestry sweep. KernelReader cannot fall back to `ps`; C27 host/argv checks remain bootstrap work. Existing legacy identity resolution still retains its prior behavior, so this is not a claim that every whole endpoint is process-free.

**Proof:** exact-head [CI 42461297831](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42461297831), successful Rust job `128670953354`, upload artifact **13609497518**: **2,260 executed cases passed**, zero failures/errors, six separately skipped. Verified 14 capability HTTP-unit cases, seven executed provenance cases, eight route-inventory cases, the real-store/socket restart integration case and all six spawn guards. Rust lint, Node22/24 and replacement delivers checks succeed. Current cap/ambiguity tests establish small-state behavior, not F001/F002's missing bounds. The ignored walk measurement was not run by this reviewer.

Clean worktree, matching local/GitHub frozen heads, CLEAN. No local builds, tests, mutation, process/SQL probe, credential-file read, restart or product edit. **AC9 live before/after launch, CPU and RSS readings remain owed at the joint A1+A2 deploy. Never bounce on A1 alone.** This verdict is about resource behavior, not a substitute for the security/correctness reviews.
